text:
Sam: heads-up — automated alert fired at 18:30UTC: p95 east-west latency between gpu-pool nodes jumped to ~320ms during the 18:25-18:29 batching window. Observed packet retransmits. Anyone digging? :eyes:
Ravi: saw it too, started at ~18:25 when batch traffic ramped. RDMA counters show tx drops on node rack-7b. Putting basic checks on it now.
Maya: can you paste the alert?
Sam: alert snippet: `ALERT p95_ew_latency > 200ms` 
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3824, severity=sev2, owner=@Sam. Logs attached (first 10 lines).
Ravi: quick checks: `ethtool -S eth0 | grep -i drop` showed `tx_errors: 0` but `rx_missed`: non-zero on the mlx5. Running `ibv_devinfo` and `ibstat` next.
Luca: ping and iperf between the two nodes?
Ravi: short iperf3 run during the window produced lots of jitter, but after 18:31 it flapped back to normal. Could be an intermittent path MTU mismatch or qdisc saturation.
Maya: any recent mtu changes or tor rollouts in that rack?
Sam: no config rollouts in the past 24h according to deploybot. Network team did a partial TOR firmware push yesterday but that was a different rack.
Ravi: dumping kernel rings: `dmesg | tail -n 40` showed repeated `mlx5_core: mlx5_cmd_mailbox_timeout` and `NETDEV WATCHDOG` for the mlx5 device. suspicious.
Maya: can you paste a sample?
Ravi: ```
[458701.123456] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: mlx5_cmd_mailbox_timeout
[458701.123460] NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (mlx5_core): transmit queue 0 blocked for 22ms
[458701.123465] device eth0 entered promiscuous mode
[458702.223000] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: FW event: port state changed to DOWN
```
Luca: FW port state change is interesting. Could this be a brief link flap on the switch side causing ARP churn?
Sam: ARP table churn would explain transient rediscovery and higher latencies. Check `arp -n` differences across nodes.
Ravi: `arp -n` consistent now, but logs show `arp_response_timeout` spikes from kernel on those hosts during window. Also saw a flood of gratuitous ARP from one NIC.
Maya: gratuitous ARP + FW port down sounds like an interface reset on one of the ToR uplinks. Any packet captures?
Ravi: grabbed a short tcpdump around 18:26: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/ew-18-26.pcap 'ether proto 0x891d or icmp or udp'` — file attached to the incident. Early look shows fragmented RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) packets and some ICMP fragmentation-needed messages.
Sam: fragmentation-needed -> PMTU issue. Are we seeing mismatched MTU on the path? Check `ip link` MTU on nodes and ToR.
Luca: ToR shows MTU 9216 on the server-facing links but the leaf switch peer toward the spine had default 1500 on one interface (config drift?). That would cause fragmentation/ICMP.
Maya: if a single hop has 1500 while others are 9k, RoCE will suffer badly. Any logs from the switch?
Sam: requested switchconfig from network team, they replied: "no global MTU change, but earlier this week a new transit link was added with default profile; automations should have set 9k but may have missed rack-7b."
Ravi: repro steps: when we force MTU 1500 on the nodes, RDMA stops flapping (but performance worse). When we set full 9216 end-to-end, things stable. So intermittent path with mixed MTU explains spikes.
Luca: For immediate mitigation we can push a BGP route dampening to favor alternate path that preserves 9k, or push a quick leaf config fix to set MTU 9k on the transit interface.
Maya: ops question — do we want to gate a rolling fix to every rack? Risk of mass config change.
Sam: propose to patch leaf for rack-7b only, run smoke tests during next low-traffic window, then monitor. Also add a short-term route preference to avoid the transit link.
Ravi: will open a playbook: `1) set MTU 9216 on leaf transit iface; 2) clear ARP cache on affected hosts; 3) restart rdma service on nodes if needed; 4) monitor p95 for 30min`
Maya: also add a guard in our infra automation to verify leaf/spine MTU consistency on changes. We should detect these mismatches in preflight.
Sam: Agreed. Can someone implement the preflight check? It should compare `ip link` MTU across path or query switch state via netconf.
Luca: I can draft the check tomorrow. For now I'm sending network team a hotfix for rack-7b and opening a change window at 22:00 UTC.
infra-bot: change request CR-2026-719 submitted for rack-7b MTU adjust, scheduled 22:00 UTC. 
Ravi: after forcing the MTU fix in a staging leaf earlier, we saw no p95 spikes for the next batch window. I'll run another controlled batch at 21:30 and post telemetry.
Maya: thanks. Can we also add RDMA error alerts (mlx5 FW events) to the oncall dashboard so we get earlier signals?
Sam: good idea — add rule for `mlx5_cmd_mailbox_timeout` and `FW event: port state changed` to infra logs alerting with low noise.
Luca: noted. I'll follow up on the playbook and preflight check PR.
Sam: thanks everyone. Closing thread when CR is applied and we see two clean batch windows. :thumbsup:
